name: Groww
tagline: India's largest retail broker: stocks, F&O, mutual funds, credit, one app
facts: 2016, Bengaluru; Lalit Keshre and three ex-Flipkart cofounders
Billionbrains Garage Ventures; NSE/BSE listed Nov 2025

strategy.label: Mission
strategy.text: Make financial services simple, transparent and accessible so every Indian can invest, trade and borrow from one app.

strategy.label: Vision
strategy.text: Become the default full-stack money app for India's next 100 million investors, from first SIP to wealth management.

strategy.label: Core strategy
strategy.text: Win acquisition with simple UX and Tier 2-3 reach, then cross-sell MTF, F&O, credit, AMC and wealth to raise ARPU.

strategy.label: Moat
strategy.text: Largest active base (29% NSE share) and low-cost organic acquisition; brand trusted by first-time investors.

strategy.label: Key bet
strategy.text: De-risk from SEBI F&O curbs: grow MTF, loans against securities, commodities, Groww AMC and Fisdom-led affluent wealth.

strategy.label: Your view
strategy.text: Is Groww a broker priced like a platform? Can it earn wealth-style margins without leaning on derivatives?

customers.pain: Finance feels complex, jargon-heavy and untrustworthy for small amounts
customers.why: Clean onboarding, zero-commission direct mutual funds, simple language and mass brand recall

customers.who: Retail F&O, intraday and commodity traders
customers.pain: Need fast execution, charts, margin and low costs during volatile sessions
customers.why: Integrated F&O, MTF and commodity trading in the same app they already use

customers.who: HNI and mass-affluent with larger portfolios
customers.pain: Fragmented holdings, little advice, liquidity locked in investments
customers.why: Fisdom wealth, loans against securities and MTF, without leaving the app

customers.who: Existing users needing personal or secured credit
customers.pain: Slow bank loans, need liquidity without selling investments
customers.why: Pre-approved personal loans and LAS from the in-house NBFC, fully digital

customers.pain: Need cheap distribution to millions of new retail investors
customers.why: Biggest retail funnel; strong SIP flows; own AMC captures fund economics

rows.how: Flat ~₹20 or 0.1% per order; F&O ~55% of Q4 FY26 revenue
Interest on margin book, client float and secured loans; ~22% of revenue
Total expense ratio on AUM; still loss-making but scaling fast
Net interest margin and processing fees from in-house NBFC

bullets.label: Revenue mix
bullets.text: Q4 FY26: equity derivatives 55%, stocks 16%, float 8%, PL+LAS 7%, MTF 5%, commodities 4%; derivatives share falling.

bullets.label: Users vs payers
bullets.text: Most MF investors pay nothing; a minority of F&O and MTF users generate the bulk of revenue.

bullets.label: Unit economics
bullets.text: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin ~68%; organic acquisition keeps CAC low; operating leverage drives profit growth.

bullets.label: Growth levers
bullets.text: MTF and commodities, affluent wealth via Fisdom, AMC scale, secured credit; reduce dependence on F&O.

bullets.label: Regulation
bullets.text: SEBI F&O curbs since Nov 2024 cut retail derivative traders ~20% in FY26; Groww hurt less than peers.

friction: App outages during market open hurt trader trust
Easy F&O access nudges novices into loss-making trades
Advanced charting weaker than Zerodha Kite for pros
Customer support slow during disputes and failed orders
Too many cross-sell prompts clutter a simple app
